dialog.body: Good morning, City of Newport Finance Department, this is Janet Whitcomb. How may I help you?
Good morning, Janet. So, I have a parking ticket that I did not exactly earn, and I'm hoping you can tell me I'm not losing my mind. Or at least that I'm losing it in an orderly fashion.
I'll do my best. May I have your name, please?
Ileana Herrera.
Thank you, Ms. Herrera. What is the situation with the ticket?

Okay. I rented a car back in October, a few days, and the rental company just sent me a letter. They forwarded me a Newport parking ticket. And it's not just the ticket, they tacked on their own fees. An administrative fee, a handling fee, I don't even know what else. It's more than the ticket itself, which is just lovely.
I understand. The rental company's fees are separate from anything the City charges. Do you have the citation number from the ticket?
I have the letter, and it's got a number on it. Hold on, my reading glasses are somewhere, probably on my head. Okay. It starts with an N, then the digits, four, four, seven, one, nine, two.
Thank you. Let me look that up. [pause] I do see a citation with that number, issued in October for an expired meter. The fine is showing as unpaid.

Right, and here's my issue. I was parked at a meter that I paid. I have the receipt from the app. So I'd like to contest it. And I'd like the City's part held while I do that, because I'm not paying the rental company's little surcharge party for something I'm disputing.
Understood. The City cannot waive or adjust what the rental company charges you. That is between you and them. As for the citation, you may submit a written appeal.
Good, that's what I want. So where do I send it? Is it an address, an email, a person? I'd like to put it in front of a real human.

It should be sent in writing to the Finance Department at City Hall, attention parking violations. Please include the citation number, your contact information, and a copy of your receipt. Please do not send the original.
Copy, not original. Got it. I've learned that lesson the hard way. Do you need the rental agreement too, since the car wasn't in my name originally?
I would include it, yes. It shows you were the driver on that date.
Okay. You know, my cousin used to have your job, believe it or not. Sat right where you're sitting. She always said people never read the back of the ticket.
Well, it is worth reading the back. The instructions for appeals are generally printed there, though yours came through the rental company, so you may not have the original.
Correct, all I got was a letter and a photocopy. Pretty sure the photocopy was made on a machine from the nineties.
If you wish, I can note on the citation that an appeal is forthcoming. You should still mail it promptly, as there are deadlines.
Yes, please note it. And what's the deadline, roughly? Am I already late? It's been a few weeks since October.
I can't confirm a deadline from this screen. I will have someone from the parking office call you back to confirm. Is 401-555-0190 the best number?
That's it, the landline. Mornings are best, though I'll take whatever I can get.
I will pass that along. Is there anything else, Ms. Herrera?
No, that's it. Thank you, Janet. I'll get the letter in the mail today, before I find another surprise fee.
Thank you for calling. Have a good day.
